findings.title: [P1] Redact provider error text before emitting calibration failures
findings.body: Provider error messages flow from the HTTP response into ProviderContextLimitError and are interpolated verbatim into stderr here. If a provider or proxy echoes a credential from the rejected payload, that credential reaches operator or CI logs. The same raw text is assigned to `message_redacted` above. The supplied `test_calibration_exit_redacts_secret_shapes_in_the_recorded_message` exercises this case, but this implementation does not redact it. Apply the existing redaction helper before logging or recording the exception.

findings.cross_file_justification: anthropic_adapter.py (diff-touched, lines 361-365 and 503-507) turns any HTTP 400/413 whose body text matches is_context_limit_message into ProviderContextLimitError, with input_tokens/limit parsed straight out of the provider's message by parse_context_limit. cheval.py's _calibration_needed_exit then persists those numbers via _ceiling_record_observed, and _lookup_max_input_tokens / the pre-flight gate consume them through _observed_for on every later invocation.
findings.description: Integers parsed from a provider (or proxy) error body become durable routing state. A single 400 response whose text says e.g. 'prompt is too long: 5 tokens > 1 maximum' writes an observed bound for (provider, model) to .run/ceiling-observed.json; test_ceiling_e2e shows the next call is then preempted at that bound with no dispatch. There is no sanity floor on `provider_limit` / `observed` visible in the diff (only `> 0`), no cap on how far a single observation may lower the catalog bound, and no expiry. The classification also runs before the billing-class check, so any 400 text containing the matched phrases is treated as a non-walkable size verdict and recorded. The `_obs` fallback uses cheval's own estimate when the provider gives no number, so a mis-classified 400 with no numbers still writes a record. routing/ceiling.py (record_observed, observed_for, the store path from LOA_CHEVAL_CEILING_OBSERVED_PATH) was truncated from this review, so clamping, symlink/atomic-write hardening of the store, and the 'only the two context classes lower the bound' claim could not be verified.
findings.failure_mode: A misbehaving upstream, an intermediary proxy, or one malformed error body permanently (until manual calibration) shrinks the usable input window for a model to an arbitrarily small value, preempting every subsequent request on that entry before dispatch — a persistent denial of service of the routing chain seeded by one untrusted response.
findings.suggested_fix: In record_observed / _calibration_needed_exit, reject observations that are below a sane floor (e.g. the 36K legacy wall or a fraction of probed_ceiling), ignore observations when provider_limit is absent instead of substituting cheval's estimate, require the parsed numbers to be mutually consistent (input_tokens > limit, limit <= context_window), add an expiry/stale_after to observed records, and only lower the bound when the HTTP status and Anthropic error `type` (e.g. invalid_request_error) agree with the message match rather than on message text alone. Verify the store write uses O_NOFOLLOW + atomic rename like ledger.py.

findings.description: The new exit path records the raw provider error text with no redaction: `"message_redacted": str(_exc)` lands in models_failed, and the same `str(_exc)` is interpolated into the `_error_json(...)` message printed to stderr. Anthropic/proxy 400 bodies can echo request fragments (and this project's own test suite at HEAD, test_calibration_exit_redacts_secret_shapes_in_the_recorded_message, asserts that a sk-ant-… token in that body must not reach models_failed or stderr — evidence that this diff shipped without the redaction and it had to be added afterwards). The envelope path is partly covered by modelinv's redact_payload_strings, but the stderr JSON is not.
findings.failure_mode: Secret-shaped or prompt-derived content from a provider error body is written verbatim to the operator log / stderr JSON (captured by orchestrator scripts and CI logs) under a field literally named message_redacted, defeating the audit chain's redaction guarantee.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass str(_exc) through the existing redaction helper (loa_cheval.config.redaction / audit.modelinv.redact_payload_strings) before placing it in models_failed and before building the _error_json message; keep the field name honest by only storing redacted text there.

findings.description: Two availability regressions in the D-1.1b short-circuit. (a) The RateLimitError arm checks only `_ceiling_unverified` and never `_e.token_limited`, so an ordinary requests-per-minute 429 on a head hop dispatched above its probed bound ends the whole invocation with RATE_LIMITED, skips the declared fallback chain, and writes a calibration record to the observed store — the HEAD test test_request_rate_429_while_unverified_walks_to_the_next_hop (BB-003) documents this as a defect. (b) `_ceiling_unverified` is set once from the head entry's pre-flight outcome and never recomputed per hop, so a 429 or provider limit on a calibrated fallback hop is misclassified as RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED / CEILING_UNVERIFIED_LIMIT and recorded against the fallback model (HEAD test test_unverified_status_is_per_hop_not_inherited_from_the_head).
findings.failure_mode: Under the opt-in ceiling policy, a transient rate limit converts into a hard failure and persistent state mutation; fallback hops are never tried, and the observed-store accumulates spurious records that feed SEC-001.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate the short-circuit on `getattr(_e, 'token_limited', False) and _hop_unverified`, where `_hop_unverified` is derived per hop (estimate vs that hop's probed/calibrated bound) rather than inherited from the head; do not write an observed record for request-rate 429s.

findings.description: `_mult` accepts any positive float, including `.inf` (valid YAML) and absurdly large values. In calculate_total_cost, `int(inp_cost * im)` raises OverflowError for inf, which happens inside create_ledger_entry after the billed call has already completed, so the row is never written and the daily spend counter is not updated. A very large but finite multiplier instead inflates cost_micro_usd and can trip the budget enforcer for every long-context call.
findings.failure_mode: A malformed or typo'd long_context block in the catalog causes post-call ledger crashes (unbilled, un-metered spend) or runaway budget exhaustion; the config loader's 'malformed means no premium' promise is not fully kept.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject non-finite values (math.isfinite) and cap multipliers to a sane range (e.g. 1.0 <= m <= 10.0), logging and falling back to 1.0 otherwise; validate the block in the config schema validator as well.

findings.description: The new GET transport builds its URL from `self.config.endpoint` and, on the urllib path, uses urllib.request.urlopen directly: it follows redirects (carrying the x-api-key header), accepts any scheme the opener supports (including file://), and reads the whole body with no size limit before json.loads. http_post has the same lineage, so this is a hardening gap rather than a new exploit, but health_check now hits it on every provider status run with the live API key attached.
findings.failure_mode: A compromised or mis-set provider endpoint in model-config.yaml (or a redirecting proxy) receives the operator's Anthropic key and can return an unbounded body to exhaust memory of the probe process.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject non-https endpoints at config validation, use an opener with redirects disabled (or strip auth headers on redirect), and cap the response read (e.g. 1 MiB) in both http_get and the urllib error branch.
